conviction_note: The print turns on two lines that point opposite ways and cannot be signed from public evidence: an unresolved GTCR take-private (Bloomberg 2026-09-11, 'coming weeks', nothing announced seven weeks on, stock $84.73 between the $77.23 pre-rumour close and Citi's ~$94 takeout estimate) and a full-year guide that needs Q4 revenue of ~$203.7M, about 8% organic growth ex-divestiture against ~6.7% implied for Q3; the quarter itself is guided to $196.3-198.3M and SPS printed above the top of its range last quarter and just under the midpoint the quarter before. Findings sum to -0.5 and p_up is 50, so the scaled number is 0; the two agree that there is no sign here, and abs_move stays at the name's own median because a deal announcement or a guide cut would each move it 10-20%.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is guided to $196.3-198.3M (midpoint $197.3M, 3-4% reported growth after ~$5M a quarter of divested 3P Revenue Recovery revenue). Record against its own range: in Q2 SPS printed $197.8M against a $194.5-196.5M guide, $1.3M above the top; in Q1 it printed $192.1M against $191.6-193.6M, $0.5M under the midpoint. Best estimate is a print at or slightly above the top of the range, about +0.4% against the $197.3-197.5M bar, which is inside what the company already guided to.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, beat above the top of the range with an underlying FY raise: +11.48% (2026-07-30). Q1 2026, at the midpoint with a reiterated FY: +4.99%. Q4 2025, at or above the guide but the FY26 guide implied deceleration: -4.37%. Over the seven prints, the reaction followed the forward guide more than the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: the guide is public and consensus sits on it. The unpriced part is only the habitual size of the beat. If the market expected a larger beat, consensus would sit above the guide midpoint, and Benzinga's $197.5M sits on it.
findings.independence: The Q1 comparison comes from a different document, the Q4 2025 release with the Q1 guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1092699/000109269926000007/er_q425.htm), and the Q1 actual from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001092699/000109269926000042/er_q126.htm. Both are company documents, so this is one company's own record, not an outside series.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide requires a steep Q4. FY midpoint $790.9M less Q1 $192.1M, Q2 $197.8M and the Q3 guide midpoint $197.3M leaves Q4 at ~$203.7M: +3.2% sequential and +5.7% reported YoY against Q4 2025's $192.7M, despite ~$5M a quarter of divested revenue, so roughly +8% organic. Q3 implies ~+6.7% organic on the same basis. Implied Q4 adj. EBITDA is ~$74M (FY mid $266.85M less $124.5M H1 less $68.4M Q3), about a 36% margin. A trimmed Q4 or FY range is the main downside path. In the Q2 release management cut the FY range by less than the $10.5M divestiture, an underlying raise of about $2.5M, and per a Quartr summary of the September Citi conference it said it was confident in high-single-digit growth. That offsets part of the risk, so it is sized small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On guidance this name has moved hard: -20.84% on 2025-10-30 and -21.99% on 2025-07-30 when the outlook disappointed, -13.80% on 2025-02-10 on a decelerating new-year guide, and +11.48% on 2026-07-30 when the underlying FY was raised. Five of the last seven prints fell.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 number is not quoted anywhere I found and has to be derived from the FY range less three quarters. Consensus pages carry only Q3 and FY. If the market were worried about the ramp, the October target raises (Citi $99, Stifel $85, Morgan Stanley $74) would not cluster just before the print. The -7.8% slide in the last five sessions is unexplained and could partly be this worry, which is one reason the size is small.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 revenue comes from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1092699/000109269926000007/er_q425.htm. Management's high-single-digit confidence comes from https://quartr.com/events/sps-commerce-inc-spsc-citi-s-2026-global-tmt-conference_ofJwt1Rc and argues against this finding. The arithmetic rests on the same Q2 release as finding 1, but on a different line (the FY guide, not the quarter).

findings.finding: The take-private is unresolved. Bloomberg reported on 2026-09-11 that GTCR was in talks to buy SPS Commerce, with a deal possible 'in the coming weeks' but nothing finalised, and said the talks could fail or another bidder emerge. The stock closed $82.68 that day, from $77.23 before the report, after an intraday $89.44. Seven weeks later there is no announcement and no 8-K after 2026-07-30 except a 13G. Spot of $84.73 sits about halfway between the $77.23 pre-rumour close and Citi's ~$94 peer-multiple takeout estimate, i.e. roughly even odds. Earnings is a natural point to announce a signed deal, which would likely move the stock +10-15%. A management statement that the process has ended, or a quiet call, would move it back toward the high $70s, -8% to -12%. Signed at its expected value, zero; it widens the move in both directions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-09-11 Bloomberg report moved the stock +7.06% at the close and +15.8% at the intraday high (https://ts2.tech/en/sps-commerce-stock-gave-back-more-than-half-its-gtcr-takeover-rally/). There is no prior earnings print held during an active sale process.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced as a probability, which is why the size is zero. What is not priced is whether it resolves inside this window. If the market expected a signing with the print, the stock would trade near $90+ as it did on 2026-10-22 ($91.94), not at $84.73 after a -7.8% five-day slide. If it expected the process had failed, it would trade nearer the $77 pre-rumour level.
findings.independence: The June sale exploration with Morgan Stanley and activist pressure (Anson, Irenic) are reported by Reuters at https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/news/sps-commerce-hires-morgan-stanley-181210898.html. findings.finding: Reuters (June 2026) reported that SPS hired Morgan Stanley as sell-side advisor on the sale. Yet Morgan Stanley's equity research raised its SPSC target to $74 from $59, keeping Underweight, around 2026-10-26. Research is normally put on restriction when the bank's advisory deal is close to signing, so an unrestricted Underweight note three days before the print weakly suggests a signing was not imminent. This is an inference, not a document.

findings.why_not_priced: Few readers will connect the advisory mandate with the research note. If priced, it would show as a fading deal premium, and the unexplained -7.8% five-day slide is consistent with that, which is a reason this is sized at almost nothing.
findings.independence: The advisory mandate is reported at https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/news/sps-commerce-hires-morgan-stanley-181210898.html. Restriction practice is not documented for this case. The finding is a proxy and inference; it shares the deal subject with finding 3 but rests on a different fact.
